Hi Elaine / Ravi —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can size a Dedicated pool and propose a path (Hosted fallback vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

Call highlights:
- You favor Dedicated capacity for predictable latency and data isolation, but want the option to burst to Hosted during peak marketing events.
- Primary model: LumenApps will run a moderately large 16k-context chat model for customer-facing assistants + a smaller reranker for search.
- Current expected steady-state: ~60 TPS per endpoint (combined), peak up to ~140 TPS for short bursts.
- SLO target: p95 latency < 600ms for short prompts, p99 < 1.5s for mixed sessions.

Clarifying asks (please confirm):
1) Token mix — can you confirm rough distribution by prompt length (short/medium/long)?
2) Concurrency per session — avg concurrent sessions vs max concurrent sessions during peak?
3) Any strict procurement constraints on GPU family (A100 vs H100) or must we include on-prem/HSM considerations for Private option?

What I'll do next:
- Share a rough capacity worksheet (attached) with GPU recommendations and a cost delta between A100/H100.
- Propose an initial Dedicated pool configuration with a Hosted fallback policy for bursts.
- Schedule a short engineering sizing call with Karthik to validate assumptions.

Attachments: capacity_worksheet_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet: traffic assumptions + perf multipliers)

Thanks — let me know the token mix and concurrency numbers and I’ll update the workbook.

Best,

Thanks Rishi — good summary; apologies for the formatting here, forwarding the answers from our infra team below.

Token mix (approx):
- Short (<= 200 tokens): 68% — chat prompts, quick completions (median ~120 tokens)
- Medium (201–1200 tokens): 24% — multi-turn context slices and system prompts (median ~650 tokens)
- Long (>1200 tokens): 8% — long-context retrieval + summarization (up to ~16k contexts)

Concurrency:
- Avg concurrent sessions during business hours: ~420 sessions (most idle/short requests)
- Max concurrent during peak campaigns: ~1,200 sessions (we expect many short requests during spikes)

TPS targets we can confirm: steady 60 TPS combined, sustained bursts up to 140 TPS for ~15–40 minutes during events.

GPU preference / procurement:
- No hard mandate, but procurement prefers not to commit to last-gen hardware for >12 months; they asked for a cost/benefit comparison A100 vs H100.
- Private VPC is a must-have option in case regulators require it later (we may start Dedicated, then convert to Private).

Questions from our side:
1) For the model you mentioned, what peak TPS per GPU are you projecting for H100 vs A100 with int8 quantization + KV cache enabled?
2) Is hybrid routing (Dedicated primary, Hosted fallback during bursts) supported out-of-the-box or does it need custom ops?

Happy to hop on a follow-up engineering call — Ravi and I are available Thursday afternoon PT.

—Elaine

Hi Elaine / Ravi —

Great, thanks for the detail — that distribution is very helpful. Below are ballpark projections and our recommended next steps. These are deliberately conservative; Karthik can validate in the sizing call.

Quick projections (model: 16k-context chat variant; assuming mixed batching + KV caching):
- H100 (80GB) with optimized kernels + int8 quant: ~18–22 TPS per GPU for mixed average worker (depends on batch depth). For short-only workloads with aggressive batching you can see 30+ TPS per GPU.
- A100 (80GB) with int8: ~12–15 TPS per GPU for mixed workloads; short-only bursts ~20 TPS.
- Reranker (smaller): can be colocated on the same pool (adds ~15% overhead) or run on cheaper T4-like instances if throughput-focused.

Recommendation for LumenApps (given token mix + concurrency):
- Start with a Dedicated pool of 4x H100 (80GB) nodes. Expected baseline throughput: ~4 * 20 TPS = ~80 TPS sustained for mixed traffic with KV cache + batching. This gives headroom for steady 60 TPS and short bursts — pair with autoscale + Hosted fallback for peaks beyond ~120–140 TPS.
- Autoscale policy: maintain min 3 nodes, scale to 8 nodes on sustained 95th percentile load > 90 TPS; allow Hosted fallback (burst routing) for spikes above 140 TPS for <1 hour windows.
- Concurrency knobs: aim for per-GPU concurrency cap ~24 simultaneous streams (depends on model memory pressure) — this keeps p95 latency tight while enabling batching benefits.
- Quantization: int8 recommended for cost reduction; run a quick eval on a labeled prompt set. If you need maximal fidelity for long-context summarization, pin a small subset of traffic to fp16 instances.

Costs & tradeoffs summary:
- H100s give ~30–50% higher throughput at ~40% higher cost vs A100; faster ROI if you care about fewer nodes and lower operator complexity.
- A100 can be cheaper per-node but will require more nodes and potentially more networking/ops overhead.

Routing & Hosted fallback:
- Hybrid routing is supported as a standard policy: we can set a policy to route overflow capacity to Redwood Hosted API with per-account burst limits. No heavy custom work required — engineering will need to validate routing for your VPC plan if you move to Private later.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik / Monica — can we schedule a 30–45m sizing call Thursday 17:00 PT (or Friday morning PT) with LumenApps to validate the worksheet and run a quick perf simulation?
2) I’ll update and attach perf_matrix_v1.csv + a revised capacity_worksheet_v2.xlsx after the call and share a draft SOW.
3) LumenApps to run a quick int8 micro-eval on ~200 representative prompts (we can provide the harness).

Attachments: perf_matrix_v1.csv; capacity_worksheet_v1.xlsx; SOW_draft_lumenapps_v0.1.pdf

Thanks — looping in Karthik and Monica to coordinate the engineering call.

Best,
Rishi
